title: Percolation thresholds and connectivity in disordered porous media
abstract: We study how randomly distributed open sites in a disordered medium suddenly connect into a system-spanning network once their density crosses a critical threshold, sharply increasing macroscopic transport. The connectivity transition is governed by local coordination and the breadth of the pore-size distribution rather than by any single channel.

title: Flattening energy landscapes accelerates barrier crossing in glassy systems
abstract: In glasses, transport is dominated by rare hops over a rugged energy landscape with a wide distribution of barriers. We show that introducing structural disorder flattens the landscape, narrowing the barrier distribution and dramatically increasing the rate of the slowest hops, which control the overall relaxation.

title: Self-limiting passivation layers in aqueous corrosion
abstract: Certain alloys form a thin surface film that stops its own growth once a few nanometres thick, because the film blocks the electronic or ionic transport that feeds further reaction. This self-limiting behaviour protects the bulk while adding minimal resistance.

title: The lotus effect: hierarchical microstructures that repel water
abstract: Water droplets bead and roll off certain leaves because a hierarchical surface microstructure traps air and minimises contact area, making the surface effectively hydrophobic without any change to the bulk material. The effect depends on surface texture and termination chemistry, not bulk composition.

title: Surface segregation in binary alloys
abstract: In many alloys one component preferentially migrates to the surface to lower surface energy, producing a terminating layer whose composition differs from the bulk. This spontaneous segregation can passivate or functionalise the surface while the bulk composition is unchanged.

title: Vibration-induced channel formation in granular media
abstract: When granular packings are vibrated, grains rearrange into transient interconnected channels that carry flow far more efficiently than the static packing. Connectivity emerges from collective rearrangement rather than from any individual large pore.

title: Funnel-shaped landscapes in protein folding
abstract: Proteins fold quickly because their energy landscape is funnel-shaped, biasing a vast number of microscopic pathways toward the native state. A smooth, biased landscape beats a flat or rugged one for reaching a target configuration fast.

title: Spin-glass ground states and frustration
abstract: Competing interactions in spin glasses create a rugged landscape of many nearly degenerate states separated by barriers. Introducing the right kind of disorder can either deepen frustration or, counter-intuitively, open low-barrier pathways between states.

title: River-network formation by erosion and self-organisation
abstract: Branching river networks self-organise to minimise total transport resistance, carving a hierarchy of channels that efficiently drains a landscape. The optimal networks share statistical features across scales independent of local geology.

title: Doping-controlled carrier concentration in semiconductors
abstract: Substituting lattice atoms with aliovalent dopants changes the number of mobile charge carriers by orders of magnitude without altering the host framework, a lever that decouples carrier concentration from carrier mobility.

title: Enzyme catalysis by transition-state stabilisation
abstract: Enzymes accelerate reactions by binding and stabilising the transition state, effectively lowering the barrier along the reaction coordinate rather than changing the reactants. Shaping the local environment around the moving species is the key lever.

title: Ant-colony optimisation and emergent shortest paths
abstract: Simple agents depositing and following a decaying signal collectively discover short paths through a network. Global efficient routes emerge from purely local reinforcement without any central plan.
